title: Visible-gap, combining-mark and compatibility-form variants of a credential
summary: Two variants of one synthetic key: a combining acute accent after its final character and its compatibility-form (fullwidth) letters. The no-break-space variant is decided in unicode-no-break-space-inside-credential-value.
rationale: Each variant differs from a plain key in a way a consumer may or may not undo: a combining mark attaches to the previous character and changes the grapheme (NFC cannot always compose it back to ASCII, so normalization is not the same as stripping it); fullwidth letters become ASCII only under NFKC, which also folds many unrelated characters. None of this is settled by the provider documents read. The no-break-space variant moved to its own case (ADR 0019 item 4).

expectation.rationale: Not asserted. No source read says a provider key survives, or is destroyed by, a combining mark or compatibility folding; UAX #15 defines the forms but does not say which one a credential reader should apply, and the engine cannot re-derive a normalize step. Kept unresolved by the maintainer (ADR 0019 item 4). What would resolve it: a source on key boundaries under normalization, or a scoped decision on normalize. Each variant is a fixture with no spans and is counted in neither TP nor FN.

sources.supports: Revision 58 (Unicode 18.0.0): defines NFC, NFD, NFKC and NFKD; ASCII-only text is unchanged by every form. Does not state that normalization removes zero-width or format characters.
The key is documented as always 69 characters; the alphabet and 22/43 segment split are tool-corroborated, not this citation. Context only: it does not mention Unicode.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Research for #96 (parent #92). Synthetic fixtures only; input facts and expectations live here, while stream APIs, limits, actual output and rejection assertions belong to downstream engine and product regression populations.
